sentences.text: The name Oryctodromeus means digger runner, derived from Ancient Greek words for digging and running. This species holds the distinction of being the first non-avian dinosaur to provide published proof of burrowing behavior.
In 2023, Oryctodromeus was officially named the state dinosaur of Idaho.
The genus was formally described by Varricchio and colleagues in 2007, with Varricchio et al., 2007 listed as the genus authority.

The type specimen, cataloged as MOR 1636a, is a partial adult skeleton containing parts of the skull, braincase, vertebrae, ribs, shoulder girdle, an arm without a hand, and leg bones. Two juvenile individuals, designated MOR 1636b, were also found and measure about 55 to 65 percent the size of the adult.

Adaptations in the jaws, forelimbs, and pelvis likely helped the animal move and manipulate soil. Additional fossils from the Wayan Formation reveal further digging adaptations located in the femur. Oryctodromeus shared a wide snout with Orodromeus and Zephyrosaurus, features that may have been used for digging.
Specimens from the Wayan Formation display a thick tendon network in the dorsal, sacral, and caudal columns, which might suggest greater flexibility in ossified tendons than previously thought.

The preserved burrow section includes two turns and smaller secondary sandstone cylinders up to a few centimeters in cross-section, likely created by smaller animals sharing the space. The burrow dimensions fit well with the probable proportions of an adult dinosaur, supporting the idea that Oryctodromeus was the burrower.
The burrow is similar to those made today by hyenas and aardwolves. The burrow was filled with sand, resulting in sandstone that stands out against the surrounding mudstone and clay.
Cladistic analysis places Oryctodromeus as basal within Euornithopoda. This analysis also revealed that the species was basal within Euornithopoda.
Oryctodromeus belongs to the family Thescelosauridae and the subfamily Orodrominae. It is a member of the class Ornithischia.

Oryctodromeus lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, specifically from the Albian to the Cenomanian ages. Fossils have been found in the Blackleaf Formation of southwestern Montana and the Wayan Formation of southeastern Idaho, dating to roughly 105 to 96 million years ago. The animal existed in the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 95 million years ago during the Cenomanian, in what is now North America. Oryctodromeus lived between 106.3 and 93.9 million years ago during the Albian to Cenomanian stages.
